---
title: 'Factoring Trust: A Machine-Checked Characterization of Where Verification Must End'
author:
  - name: Timothy DeHerrera
    affiliations:
      - name: Cyphrpunk LLC
    email: timothy@cyphrpunk.com
abstract: |
  Every deployed verification system ships a trusted remainder — a
  certificate authority, a genesis seed, a witness quorum — and the
  literature that studies each such system formalizes what can be
  *established* while leaving the remainder assumed, listed, and never
  analyzed. We give that remainder a shape. We show that trust is
  exactly the complement of verifiability and that, above a floor of two
  named residuals, the complement *factors*: verification of a claim
  over a growing, append-only record fails for exactly one of three
  reasons — the claim is not determined by the record, the record does
  not certify it at the verifier's computational power, or the claim
  does not survive the record's growth — and each failure names whom the
  verifier must trust and what repairing it costs. The "exactly" is not
  a taxonomy but a machine-checked biconditional, proved in Lean 4 across
  a tower of verifier strata (oracle, computable; the polynomial stratum
  remains an open conjecture). A companion theorem — the verification
  ceiling — generalizes the same trichotomy from append-only records to
  any well-founded justification structure, and we instantiate it twice,
  once as a cryptographic identity system and once as a follow-up
  source-integrity system, to demonstrate that the factoring, and not
  merely one instance of it, is the contribution. Every ingredient of
  this factoring is independently attested in the literature — the
  observables-frame algebra of synthetic topology, CALM's
  monotonicity-coordination biconditional, archival diplomatics'
  empirically tested determination hypothesis — but no source we reached
  composes them, or names their common complement as trust.
date: 2026-07-24
---
